chapter: The Blue Room and Lou Forbes band
title: Lou Forbes band, Blue Room's end and Blue Hawaiian Room
summary: Forbes led the band until the room closed at the end of 1931; Hirsch names Forbes band members.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: So you say Lou Forbes had the band in there until it closed then, huh? When did it close? What year?

Well, when did I say when did it open? You said in 31. Well, it closed about in 30, 30, closed the end of 31. Uh-huh, okay. This is some of the band, yeah. When did it reopen again? The next day. The next day, okay. They changed his name to the Blue Hawaiian Room.

This is Forbes' band. This is Forbes here. I'm going to play the Gentle Motor Show at the other time. Here's Forbes. Red Bowman. Menatana. He's dead. Chory Horton is dead. I can go right through the line. Johnny Roanagan. That's my wife. What are you saying? Nanny Powers. This is the only guy that I don't know who if he's alive or dead. Chester Wick is dead. Is that a trumpet player that you don't know about? No, a violin player. Violin player.
Mm-hmm. Chester Wicker was a piano player?
I never did know him. This is when Gordon had the orchestra.
